Rockot through the atmosphere

T+0 

Atmosphere

Altitude on a log scale, so the thin lower layers stay visible. Temperature: US Standard Atmosphere 1976.

Altitude

Speed relative to the air

Dynamic pressure ½ρv²

Speed rises while density falls: their product peaks at max-Q, the largest aerodynamic load.

Forces

Thrust grows as the air thins (less back pressure on the nozzles); drag is ½ρv²·CD·A.

Where the Δv goes

Max-Q 68 kPa at 11.1 km, 52 s. Losses to the end of the replay: gravity 987 m/s, drag 99 m/s, back pressure 67 m/s.

Pitch stability

Rockot has no fins: its lift acts near the nose (Barrowman slender-body method), well ahead of the centre of gravity, so the bare airframe is unstable and the engines must steer it straight. The CG moves as the tanks drain from the top and as stages and the fairing drop.

Positions measured aft from the nose tip.

Static margin

(xCP − xCG) / diameter, in calibers; negative is unstable. Shown where q > 200 Pa.

Pitch divergence: time to double

How fast an uncorrected pitch disturbance grows: aerodynamic stiffness against pitch inertia, with aerodynamic and exhaust-jet damping. Shortest near max-Q, where the steering must be fastest.

Steering needed

Engine deflection that holds 1° of angle of attack (moment balance). Static margin -6.1 to -2.6 calibers: the CP is ahead of the CG throughout, so the airframe alone is unstable. The fastest divergence is at 52 s, doubling every 0.42 s. The CG moves 6.0 m over the stage 1 burn.

Trajectory and attitude

Earth-fixed, from the launch site; the dashed line is the ground track on the curved Earth. Glyphs show the body axis every few seconds; drag to turn, scroll to zoom.

Angle of attack (6-DOF)

The angle between the body axis and the airflow, from the six-degree-of-freedom flight: the pitch kick, the tracking of the gravity turn, and the wind. After stage 1 separation the upper stage yaws to take out the sideways velocity the wind drift left, briefly flying sideways through the thin air. Blank where q < 200 Pa. Largest load: q·α 297 kPa·deg at 50 s (4.5° in 35 m/s of wind at 10.1 km), gimbal 2.0° at most through max-Q.

Wind

Aerodynamic load q·α

Dynamic pressure times angle of attack: the index launch vehicles are designed to (bending load on the structure).

Engine gimbal

Nozzle deflection the autopilot commands to hold the attitude against the aerodynamic moment (limit 7°, 20°/s).

Autopilot stability margins

python-control on the linearised pitch loop (airframe, actuator, autopilot, 30 ms of sensing and computing delay), every 2 s. Gain margins: how much the loop gain may rise or fall before the vehicle goes unstable. At max-Q: phase margin 38°, gain margins +17 / -12 dB; the closed loop is stable at 100 % of the 528 points checked.

Events

    Rockot / Breeze-KM model drawn from published dimensions (29.15 m, 2.5 m stages, 2.62 m fairing); colours and details approximate. Flight: the first-principles model on the Rockot page. Earth and sky: a single-scattering atmosphere shader; the ground is procedural.
